VIAGOGO - ticket reselling

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We explore how ticket resellers make huge profits while eager sport and music fans are left disappointed at popular events, told that their tickets are either invalid or never existed to begin with.

Unique Selling Point:
We visit the Viagogo website and show viewers the flaws in the system and how exactly a buyer can end up paying as much as five times the value of an event ticket in some cases.



Summary:
Viagogo is an online event ticket sales platform. Its headquarters are in Switzerland and it operates in more than 160 countries across the globe. Ticket reselling in most countries is allowed if a small volume of tickets are sold and at cost price e.g. if a person has bought a ticket or two to an event they can no longer attend, it is acceptable for that person to resell the ticket. However, what Viagogo does is to go to reliable ticket sellers such as Computicket, buy tickets in bulk and essentially “sell out” the event. Thereafter Viagogo skyrockets the prices and resells the same tickets for exorbitant amounts.



Further information:
The issues with Viagogo are the following:

1> They claim the tickets are already sold out or selling out fast, even when they are still available at official sellers.
2> For certain big events, they claim to be the official seller of tickets.
3> They hike the prices by adding handling and booking fees which vary per ticket sold, with no clear explanation as to what those additional charges cover.
4> Viagogo is accused of taking money for tickets even when none are available and the event really has sold out.
5> Viagogo customer service is inaccessible to locals meaning there are no contact details for a platform where buyers can direct their queries or complaints.

Our insert will show exactly how the Viagogo website works. We also make reference to international headlines about Viagogo processes as well as give examples of other websites similar to Viagogo including the popular Instaticket site.

PLEASE NOTE: We are excluding the NCC because, after our discussions with them, they are not even aware of ticket reselling on as massive a scale as Viagogo and have received no complaints – and as such, will not add much value to the insert currently. Also, we are also excluding Computicket because for the longest time they have had limits of tickets sold to each individual to reduce ticket reselling and other than that, they have nothing else to add.

FINAL TICKET RESELLING SCRIPT



AUDIO

PUMLA MNCWANGO – RUGBY FAN – NEW FOOTAGE



I thought there is a Rugby World Cup in Japan, tickets are going like hotcakes, I might end up not getting any tickets.

MPHO MUTLOANE – TENNIS FAN – RAW

It's the two greatest tennis players that ever lived. I wanted court-side seats.

PIERRE LE GRANGE – MUSIC FAN – NEW FOOTAGE



We've attended all the shows since 2012. I decided that I would like to book some tickets for the show.

VO - Eager fans will do anything to get their hands on tickets to see their favorite icons. But things don't always go as planned...



In the Eastern Cape, avid rugby supporter Pumla Mncwango went online in December last year to buy tickets for South Africa's first match of the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan.

PUMLA MNCWANGO – RUGBY FAN



I went on Google and I typed in Rugby World Cup 2019 tickets, then there was this site that popped up, Viagogo.

VO – Viagogo is a popular ticket reselling platform that operates a network of sixty websites that service clients in over one hundred and sixty countries, including South Africa.



There is no law against ticket reselling specifically but official agencies and event organisers can choose to put restrictions on tickets.



Pumla purchased tickets on Viagogo.

PUMLA MNCWANGO – RUGBY FAN



00:41:05:19 – I paid about fourteen thousand for 2 tickets.

VO - Pumla spent another twenty-six thousand rands on flights and accommodation. In August, a worrying message on the Rugby World Cup website shocked her.

PUMLA MNCWANGO – RUGBY FAN



I saw a warning on that official site, saying people who bought tickets the companies that were listed there … that if you bought tickets from those sites, you won't be allowed access into the stadium. Viagogo was one on the top of that list. I had to cancel my flight tickets. I got a penalty of R1 750 per ticket. Then I relisted the tickets but I got a refund of about R4 000 less than what I have paid. Then accommodation I paid about R7 800.

VO – Pumla says that the only way she could get any money back was to resell the tickets on Viagogo for less than what she paid.



Of the forty thousand rands she spent on the entire trip, Pumla lost more than fifteen thousand rands in cancellation fees.



Online business expert, Arthur Goldstuck says there are many complaints about resellers.

ARTHUR GOLDSTUCK – ONLINE BUSINESS EXPERT



People have felt that they have been ripped off primarily by high prices to the extent that there is a Facebook group that's called Victims of Viagogo.

UPSOUND



Rafael vs Federer Supersport archives

LINK – Roger Federer versus Rafael Nadal- it's a dream match for any tennis fan so it comes as no surprise that thousands of people were online ready to buy tickets the minute they came on sale for the much anticipated clash in Cape Town in February next year.

UPSOUND – MPHO PODCAST

The most expensive ticket was R2 000, the cheapest ticket was R150. Twenty minutes goes by, we're not being allowed in and then we're told: “No, tickets are already sold out. They were sold out by ten past nine.”

VO – And that's how the excitement was snuffed out for Joburg's Mpho Mutloane, a tennis fan and sports podcaster.

Tickets sold out in ten minutes.

The official ticketing company may have sold out, but it was a different story on other websites.

MPHO MUTLOANE – TENNIS FAN

And you see these tickets going for six, some even ten times more.

VO – According to Mpho, that was for seats rights at the back of the venue.

MPHO MUTLOANE – TENNIS FAN

But I'm not paying four thousand rands to sit in the nosebleed seats and not get a little, at least even a ball hit to me or a cap thrown at me or something like that.

LINK – Ticket reselling websites have been accused of buying tickets in bulk from official agents so the event is effectively sold out, and then reselling those tickets at sky-high prices to desperate buyers.

VO – In a statement to us, the Roger Federer Foundation warns against resold tickets as it cannot guarantee their validity.

In response to these allegations, Viagogo says it does not sell or buy tickets, neither does it set prices. It's only a platform for buyers and sellers to transact. Sellers set the prices and the buyers determine if those prices are suitable.

It is indeed possible that fraudsters, who sell non-existent and invalid tickets, take advantage of the platform without Viagogo's knowledge.

ARTHUR GOLDSTUCK – ONLINE BUSINESS EXPERT

It's very easy to say you're a platform but they do have to take responsibility . They do have to be good corporate citizens.

VO – Viagogo says that it guarantees that if a customer has a problem with a ticket, they will either find replacement ticket or give a full refund. They added that they take vetting sellers on their website very seriously and sellers only get paid after a buyer attends the event.

LINK – Despite official confirmation that tickets are no longer available, on Viagogo we found plenty, starting at eight thousand rands, and for a mere forty-seven thousand, you can be in the grandstand to watch Raf and The Fed go head-to-head.

VO – Viagogo says sellers are in charge of setting the prices and where there is a high demand for an event, the prices increase. Tickets that are listed at unreasonable prices get the most media attention but rarely, if ever, sell.

LINK – 01:20:49:21 - “Less than 1% of total tickets in the venue currently available on our site.” Now that's a message to whip any fan into a ticket buying frenzy and strangely enough, always just 1 ticket remaining.

VO – Viagogo says alerts about tickets being sold out relate solely to Viagogo where there aren't any more tickets available – tickets may be available elsewhere.


Popup messages like these led Pierre le Grange to believe tickets were running out and he paid a hefty price for him and his family to enjoy this year's Afrikaans is Groot festival.

PIERRE LE GRANGE – MUSIC FAN

I can remember an amount of about one thousand on hundred rand and I assume that that is the total value of all 5 tickets and when the transaction went through, the total amount was I think over seven thousand six hundred something rands for the 5 tickets.

VO – Pierre only realised that the total charge for the tickets was higher than initially quoted after he completed the transaction. Through official sales agents, he would have paid no more than R450 per stub.


Viagogo says it has made changes to clarify the estimated value of the ticket earlier in the buying transaction, but it does display the final purchase price clearly before the buyer has completed their purchase.

Brendon Hargroves represents Coleske Artists, one of the organisers of the Afrikaans is Groot festival. According to him, thousands of fans were disappointed when they tried to enter last year's concert.

BRENDON HARGROVES – COLESKE ARTISTS

00:03:05:11 – Our conservative estimate is that we had nearly three and half thousand people arrived here with duplicate or false Viagogo tickets.

VO – Hargroves says in 2018, many of the people who bought the Afrikaans concert tickets received stubs with no seat numbers.

BRENDON HARGROVES – COLESKE ARTISTS

00:05:44:12 – We have made people duly aware that they shouldn't buy tickets through third parties.

VO – Viagogo responded that its records confirmed that three hundred and twenty-one customers purchased tickets to the concert last year and only one customer informed them that they were turned away.

LINK – The Afrikaans is Groot 2019 concert starts at this venue, the Sun Arena in Pretoria, on the 22nd of November and only then will the organisers know if their efforts to warn the public against resold tickets have been effective.

VO – After social media complaints, in July this year, Google removed Viagogo from its top paid-for results, citing contravention of the search engine's advertising policy. A move that Viagogo is appealing.

This intervention came too late for Pumla.

PUMLA MNCWANGO – RUGBY FAN

I would like to warn people about this Viagogo. I don't want someone to be a victim.



PROMOS

Imagine buying an expensive ticket for a much-anticipated event, only to find out when you arrive at the gate that your ticket is not valid.

Event tickets sold out within minutes but available on reselling websites for as much as ten times the original price – we investigate how resellers operate.

Tickets sold out within ten minutes – we investigate how some websites are running a lucrative business selling tickets for as much as ten times the original price.

metadata.Further information: The issues with Viagogo are the following: 1> They claim the tickets are already sold out or selling out fast, even when they are still available at official sellers. 2> For certain big events, they claim to be the official seller of tickets. 3> They hike the prices by adding handling and booking fees which vary per ticket sold, with no clear explanation as to what those additional charges cover. 4> Viagogo is accused of taking money for tickets even when none are available and the event really has sold out. 5> Viagogo customer service is inaccessible to locals meaning there are no contact details for a platform where buyers can direct their queries or complaints. Our insert will show exactly how the Viagogo website works. We also make reference to international headlines about Viagogo processes as well as give examples of other websites similar to Viagogo including the popular Instaticket site. PLEASE NOTE: We are excluding the NCC because, after our discussions with them, they are not even aware of ticket reselling on as massive a scale as Viagogo and have received no complaints – and as such, will not add much value to the insert currently. Also, we are also excluding Computicket because for the longest time they have had limits of tickets sold to each individual to reduce ticket reselling and other than that, they have nothing else to add.
